what_happened: Research confirmed the Write-tool path already resolves markers whole-file correctly today (tool_input.content IS the full new file); only the Edit path has the snippet-only defect. This narrowed the fix to one path plus a depth-counter upgrade in the shared library, and let the Write-side test cases be framed as regression guards rather than new feature work.

Planning discovered that the research report's recommended depth-counter + validity tightening of strip_exempt_regions is NOT behavior-preserving on the current tree: five source-store test files (test-check-task-references.sh, test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, test-git-commit-phase.sh, test-git-commit-scoped.sh, test-orchestrate-record-decision.sh) end their marker parse at eof_depth>0, partly from redundant nested begins and partly because PROSE that merely mentions the literal token is itself parsed as a marker. Under the new rule those files' trailing regions become scannable and the repo-wide lint would go red. The plan therefore adds a marker-hygiene remediation phase ahead of the library change, which the research report did not anticipate.

A single awk depth-trace one-liner over git ls-files pinpointed every imbalanced marker file and its first unclosed begin line in one pass, converting an unbounded 'which files might break' worry into a closed five-file list with exact line numbers before any code was written. The same one-liner is reusable as the plan's own verification command and as the basis for the new library balance-report function.
